sections.h2: How has Nicholasville grown, and what does it mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Jessamine County's seat, Nicholasville, is a home rule city lying south of Lexington. It counted 28,015 residents in 2010 and 31,093 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimated 33,857 on July 1, 2025, a rise of 8.8 percent over the 2020 base. Between 1970 and 2020 the population grew by about 440 percent, which makes it the tenth most populous city in Kentucky.

Growth like that means a lot of the housing is relatively recent and a lot of owners are commuters. The 2020-2024 Census figures show 12,131 households, an owner-occupied rate of 58.2 percent, a median home value of $226,800 and a mean commute of 24 minutes.

sections.h2: What is the setting of a Nicholasville house?
sections.html:
The town was founded in 1798 and incorporated in 1837, named for a colonel who helped shape Kentucky's first constitution. Downtown sits about six miles south of the Fayette County line, and the city covers roughly 13 square miles of land. A partly channelized stream called Town Fork runs underneath downtown and drains to Jessamine Creek, and there are small artificial ponds such as Lake Mingo.

The Bluegrass climate is humid subtropical at its northern edge, with hot, humid summers, cool winters and four distinct seasons. Camp Nelson National Monument is close by, the Young House carries a National Register listing, and the Kentucky Wine and Vine Fest was named the official wine festival of Kentucky by the General Assembly in 2014.

  • Nicholasville is a logistics and commuter link between Lexington and Garrard County.
  • Jessamine County Schools provides public education, including Nicholasville, Brookside, Red Oak, Rosenwald-Dunbar and Hattie C. Warner elementary schools.
  • City government is a commission of a mayor and four commissioners, elected at large, who also run city departments.

sections.h2: Who handles code complaints and permits in Nicholasville?
sections.html:
Nicholasville has its own Code Enforcement office at 717 N. Main Street, and complaints go in through a form on the city website. A Code Enforcement Board also hears matters, and residents can apply to serve on it. If you have received a notice about tall grass, debris or an unsafe structure, answer it before you list or accept an offer.

For building and electrical permits, ask the city Planning and Zoning office which approvals your project needs, and keep copies of finished permits to hand to a buyer. Unpermitted work is a common reason a conventional sale stalls, so tell a buyer about it up front.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about owning a house in Nicholasville?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau reports median selected monthly owner costs of $1,410 for Nicholasville owners with a mortgage and $507 for those without one. Median gross rent is $1,147 a month. Median household income is $68,503 and about 13.1 percent of residents live in poverty, while 26.9 percent of adults aged 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree.

The 2020 census counted 12,356 housing units, of which 4.8 percent were vacant, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 1.2 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 4.9 percent. Few owner-occupied houses stood empty. About 36.5 percent of households include children under 18, the median age was 35.7, and the average household has 2.63 people, which fits a family-oriented commuter town.

Retail sales in the city totaled $976,312,000 in 2022, or $30,554 per capita, compared with $23,150 per capita for Lexington-Fayette. City commission meetings take place twice a month, and a seller with a rezoning or street question can ask the city for the next meeting date.

sections.h2: What does the Jessamine County Clerk do when a Nicholasville house sells?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for the city are recorded by the Jessamine County Clerk, who also keeps the county's property records. The main office, at 101 North Main Street, is open Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and a branch in Wilmore keeps shorter hours. Call (859) 885-4161.

Before accepting a deed, the clerk collects the state transfer tax under KRS 142.050. The seller pays 50 cents for each $500 of price. Five percent of collections stays with the clerk as a fee, and the rest goes to the county treasurer.

Gifts and nominal-price deeds from a parent to a child escape the tax, as do tax sales, foreclosures and deeds given in lieu of foreclosure.

sections.h2: What should a Nicholasville owner know about property tax?
sections.html:
The Jessamine County PVA assesses real estate for the county, and its site announced that the homestead and disability exemption for 2025-2026 is $49,100. Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, can apply through the PVA, and the exemption lowers the taxable value rather than the bill itself.

The closing agent usually divides the year's bill between buyer and seller, so request the proration math ahead of time. If a bill on an inherited house has gone unpaid, ask the County Clerk's delinquent tax desk for the amount owed before you agree on a closing date.

sections.h2: When is a cash offer a good fit for a Nicholasville house?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits an owner who values a firm date over the last few thousand dollars. With 33,857 residents there are plenty of buyers, yet a house with problems can still linger.

  • A home from an estate, with heirs far away and no appetite for fixing it up.
  • A rental whose tenant has left, leaving work to be done before it can be shown.
  • A property carrying a code complaint or work done without a permit.
  • An owner relocating on a short timeline to or from the Lexington area.

Owners relocating for a Lexington-area job often work to a fixed date, and a cash deal can close on the day you pick. Get terms in writing, check the net against a listing after repairs and agent costs, and have the title company confirm the payoff before you accept.

faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 31,093 residents, and the Census Bureau estimated 33,857 for July 1, 2025. Land area is about 14.6 square miles.

faqs.q: Where is a Nicholasville deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Jessamine County Clerk, 101 North Main Street, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The transfer tax is collected there first.

faqs.q: What is the tax on a $226,800 Nicholasville sale?
faqs.a: $227. The rate is 50 cents per $500 of price, 454 units after rounding up, and the seller pays under KRS 142.050.

faqs.q: What if I get a code notice in Nicholasville?
faqs.a: Use the form on the city's Code Enforcement page or visit 717 N. Main Street. Respond to a notice before you agree to a closing date.

faqs.q: Does Jessamine County offer a tax break for older owners?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners aged 65 or over, or disabled, can apply through the PVA for the homestead exemption, listed at $49,100 for 2025-2026. It lowers assessed value rather than the bill.
